q: Can a user's email be hidden while their profile stays public?
a: Not today. firestore.rules line 22 grants every signed in user read of the whole users/{uid} document and UserProfile.email sits on it at firestore.types.ts line 7. Consent gated email means moving it under users/{uid}/data, the same move the Replicate key already took.

q: How are resources linked to each other across the app?
a: A tag system carrying the descriptors. Tags link lore, docs, objects, places and npcs together, and are what makes generating a character sheet, its images and a play loop recommendation possible. Nothing of it exists; CharacterMetadata.tags is the only tags field today and nothing reads it. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: What does sharing a character mean?
a: A link. The recipient opens a read only view of the sheet, rendered by a viewing mode of the character creator, and then chooses to copy it into their own. Share is the link, copy is the snapshot, and the viewer is a surface that does not exist yet. Decided by the user 2026-09-06.

q: What is an encounter meant to become?
a: A 2D battle map. Combatants, npcs and objects are pieces moved on a shared map, the encounter is marked on the map so a player sees where they stand, and proximity can be turned on. Combatants group into sides, a turn tracker runs, and each character's turn shows its available actions as clickable items with recommendations. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: What chat surfaces does the app owe?
a: Three. A campaign channel, a direct chat between two users, and temporary secret breakout chats between a subset of a campaign's members. Today only the campaign channel exists, at campaigns/{id}/chat gated on membership. Decided by the user 2026-09-06.

q: Does a campaign own its maps, npcs, locations and quests?
a: No longer. Every resource is created independently in its own folder, searchable on its own, and shared into a campaign by link with edit rights granted to users or campaigns. The campaign brings them together and the DM controls reveal. This replaces the four subcollections data.md describes. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: How is a player found and shown in the discover directory?
a: Searched by username or email, but email is never revealed until that user consents on their own screen. A row shows portrait and username only. The portrait loads only while the peer is online to seed it, so presence must exist outside a campaign; peers today sit under campaigns/{id}/peers. Decided 2026-09-06.

q: Who appears in the discover directory and how do two players connect?
a: Every signed in user, no opt out, searchable by the whole app. Decided by the user on 2026-09-06. Connection is a friend request: one player sends, the other accepts, and friendship is what the discover area is built on. firestore.rules line 22 already lets any signed in user read any profile.

q: Does the app have a discover area where players find each other?
a: No, and the user wants one: a global directory to inspect another player's pages, invite to chat and to a campaign, and share or copy a character or campaign. No invite exists anywhere, and firestore.rules line 73 lets only the DM write a campaign, so no player can self join without a rules change.

q: What is the reference for the campaign map?
a: Legend Keeper, named by the user on 2026-09-06, with additions on top. The existing model already matches it: zoom banded layers and markers, nested maps via link_map_id, and pins carrying record_kind and record_id rather than prose. MapCanvas.svelte does wheel zoom, pointer drag, layer pick by zoom and the is_visible reveal filter.

q: How does a tester wave run so the dev server and the gate are not rerun per task?
a: Agents write tests in parallel and execute nothing. The session runs the gate once for the whole wave through task.sh run, which holds one execution lock per checkout, and task.sh serve reuses the one dev server. task.sh land takes several ids and puts the wave in one commit, so a test that reached another task's code fails visibly.

q: Where does a failed task go, and where does the failing output live?
a: Failed is the worker's queue beside staged and task.sh next prints it first; the task keeps its base and a new agent field so the agent that wrote the code fixes it. Staged is the human handoff, never a failure lane. Failing output goes to test/<id>/ via task.sh result; Findings is one line per defect naming that file.

q: Is the first gothic design pass what the user wants the app to look like?
a: No. On 2026-09-06 the user called the panel frames broken, text size unhandled and off the theme, the top bar due for a complete redesign, and everything looking weird. Colouring, theming, texture, frames, design and completeness all need to be far better, starting from a second round of fantasy UI inspiration found online and written into docs/inspiration/README.md.

q: Does dndcs have an encounter or initiative data model?
a: Yes, since 104 and 105 landed. firestore.types.ts carries CampaignEncounter and EncounterCombatant, with CombatantKind covering 'npc'; campaignService exposes postEncountersListener. MainMenu.svelte renders the tracker from that model in initiative order, so the honest empty state now only shows when no campaign or no live encounter is present.

q: What happens to the worker watch when /clear is run in a resting worker terminal?
a: The watch.sh worker --wait process survives /clear under the same claude process and keeps .git/lcp/worker.pid, so a second --wait is refused with 'worker is already waiting in this repo'. Its wake no longer reaches the cleared conversation. The user kills the old pid or types /lcp-worker again when the board moves; the session may not kill it itself.

q: Should the tool buttons in the bar vary their sigil frames?
a: No. The user on 2026-09-06 called the mixed plate, star, cusped, lobed and ring frames in the sheet bar random and wants every bar tool the same design, drawn from docs/inspiration/8.png, the forged HUD with circular sigil buttons. Only the glyph inside differs between two bar tools; the frame is decided once, not per call site.

q: Does the user want any fixed pixel size in the dndcs UI?
a: No. The user wants every size dynamic: a token from src/app.css, a fraction of the container or a clamp, never a fixed pixel width or height. Stated during the 110 browser walk on 2026-09-06 and the reason 127 strips fixed sizes from the sheet; a hairline border is the one exception.

q: What did the user find wrong with the character sheet on 2026-09-06?
a: Overflow with no dynamic resizing, uneven oversized buttons off the inspiration layouts, panels grouped oddly with weak frames, portrait frames far simpler than the reference, and dialogs seen off centre. The sheet should take much more from docs/inspiration.

q: How should layout sizes be set across the app?
a: Nothing is fixed anywhere: every panel, board, dialog and button is sized dynamically from the viewport and its content, never a fixed pixel width or height. Stated by the user on 2026-09-06 after seeing the sheet board overlap the ability column with a drawer open.

q: Where does the reference text and art for class and race documents come from?
a: D&D Beyond, named by the user on 2026-09-06 as the reference the table uses for classes, races, their content and images. The fetched set lives under reference/dndbeyond/, gitignored and never shipped, pulled by scripts/reference.sh through just reference <kind>. Documents under public/sources stay hand authored and nothing is generated from the set.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?

The Chrome extension is never used; the user rewrote 110 by hand in commit afa9aab on 2026-09-06.

q: Which account signs in for the browser walk?
a: The test user sub@slytech.no, held as WALK_EMAIL and WALK_PASSWORD in .env.

q: Which browser and driver does browser verification use?
a: playwright with Brave, through the playwright MCP and playwright-cli. The Chrome extension and the claude-in-chrome tools are never used again.

a: Two env keys, an email and a password, added to .env and .env.example without a VITE_ prefix since they are secrets. The walk fills #login-email and #login-password from them against the live project. The account owns a character named Testy and a campaign.

q: Should the worker agent that 110 was dispatched to write the playwright-cli walk under test/ now, leaving the extension walk and the findings to the solo session that q-001 named, or should 110 stay untouched until the worker session takes it solo?
a: The agent writes nothing. Task 110 is taken solo by the worker session in the main conversation, which does both halves: the playwright-cli walk under test/ and the extension walk with the findings, because only the solo session holds the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools and one scope lands as one commit.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?
a: Both. 110 runs solo in a worker session with the Chrome extension paired for the visual walk, and the same session runs playwright-cli, installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/playwright-cli, as the scripted driver. The user asked for both on 2026-09-06; the earlier answer of no headless driver is superseded.

q: Which elements are duplicated on the sheet in the second screenshot, taken after 113 and 115 landed? The image shows the six ability boxes, the six saving throw tiles, the skills table and the stat boxes once each, so the duplicate is not visible in the frame sent.?

q: What supplies the twenty three pieces of catalogue art: SVG emblems authored in the repo's own Ornament idiom, or raster files you drop under public/ yourself?
a: Author the twenty three pieces as SVG emblems in the repo's own Ornament idiom, under public/sources/art/ and addressed as plain paths. The repo already draws its whole ornamental vocabulary as inline SVG in Ornament.svelte and Sigil.svelte, nothing in the app generates raster art, and an emblem set stays consistent with the gothic language the pages carry.

q: Should 110 run solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired, or should it carry a headless driver a worker agent can run instead?
a: Run 110 solo in the main conversation with the Chrome extension paired. The walk needs a rendered page and a signed-in Firebase session, and the main conversation is the only context that holds the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools, so no headless driver is added and no new task is created.

q: How is a die roll recorded?
a: writeRollLog(type, text, formula, roll, total, details) in engine.ts. formula is passed at each of the ten call sites, never regexed from display text. RollLogItem adds author, set only on entries read back from the shared campaign log, so ChatItem renders it as a field.

q: Where does the shared campaign chat and roll log live?
a: campaigns/{id}/chat/{entryId}: author_id, author_name, kind (message|roll), body, query, is_hidden, roll_kind, formula, dice, roll, total, created_at. campaignService.postChatListener orders by created_at. getChatLog() in chat.ts scopes off currentRoute into currentCampaignId, mirrors local rollStore and replicateStore appends up, and falls to localStorage when no campaign is in scope.

q: Does dndcs have an encounter or initiative data model?
a: No. firestore.types.ts carries Campaign, CampaignSession, CampaignQuest, CampaignNpc, CampaignLocation, CampaignMap and MapMarker only; campaignService exposes no encounter call and COLLECTIONS names no encounter collection. The MainMenu Encounter tracker section renders an honest empty state until one is defined.

q: Why does a Button focus ring vanish in dndcs ui primitives?
a: clip-path on an element clips its own outer box-shadow, so var(--focus-ring) on a clipped root is invisible. The fix used in src/components/ui/Button.svelte, Slot.svelte and Stat.svelte: keep the interactive root unclipped (background: none) and hold the silhouette in a --*-shape custom property applied via clip-path to absolutely positioned frame/face/sheen layers. The root then carries box-shadow: var(--focus-ring) normally.

q: How are classes and races modelled?
a: Identically. src/lib/catalog.ts is the one loader for both kinds: getCatalog(kind), getCatalogEntry(kind, id), postCatalogReading(kind, sources) and getCatalogFacts(kind, entry). Documents are public/sources/classes/*.json and public/sources/races/*.json with an index.json per directory listing ids. There is no built-in versus custom distinction: an uploaded class is read into the same shape, cached by putCatalogEntry, and sits in the same list. src/components/CatalogList.svelte is the one vertical picker both steps use, carrying the define-your-own upload row and a link to /sources/:kind/:id. The create flow is character then class then race, and the race step is the one that writes the character.

q: Where does the ability list on the create page come from?
a: public/sources/systems/<id>.json attributes, loaded with getSystem. It is never a const in a component: gunslinger.json already declares a 7th attribute grt, and engine.md forbids hard coding a system. CharacterCreatePage renders one box per declared attribute, evaluates the declared modifier expression with getExpressionValue, and carries its own added attributes on creationData.attributes so the character can declare one nobody else has. getAbilities already takes Record<string, number> so an arbitrary id set needs no change downstream.

q: Why does the firebase cli crash on this machine?
a: Node v26.7.0 removed SlowBuffer, and buffer-equal-constant-time@1.0.1 reads SlowBuffer.prototype at module load. firebase-tools 14.10.1 reaches it through jwa. Updating does not help: jwa@2.0.1 still depends on buffer-equal-constant-time@^1.0.1 and 1.0.1 is still the latest release. Run firebase under Node 22, or publish rules from the Firebase console. The binary is at ~/Library/pnpm/firebase and is not on the default PATH.

q: How does a file reach another player?
a: src/lib/swarm.ts, torrent style. The file: record carries blocks, an array of SHA-256 base64 hashes of the original split at 64KB, plus block_size. Presence sits at campaigns/{id}/peers/{uid}.{session} with a 20s beat and a 60s stale cutoff, signalling at campaigns/{id}/signals, deleted as read, lower peer id offers. Firestore carries presence only: availability is asked over the data channel with have?/have, blocks with want and a binary frame prefixed by a 4 byte request id. Each block is verified against its hash and a failing block is asked of the next holder. count 0 means no floor so the swarm is awaited, otherwise the floor renders at once and the original is pulled in the background into media/. No TURN, so a symmetric NAT pair falls back to the floor.

q: How does a player run dndcs?
a: Each player clones the repo and runs just dev. The dev server is part of the product: the /replicate proxy reaches the API without CORS, and the /media/ store in vite.config.ts reads and writes real files under media/ (gitignored) with ETag, If-None-Match and byte ranges. This replaced the frontend only and static rule in setup.md. A hosted dist still builds but has neither proxy nor media store, so AI and full size media need the local client.

q: How are uploaded files stored without Cloud Storage?
a: postFile downscales an image to 1600px WebP q0.82, tries Cloud Storage, and on failure writes base64 in 500KB pieces to Firestore under users/{uid}/files/{id}/chunks/{n} or campaigns/{id}/files/{id}/chunks/{n}, returning a chunks: address. The head document carries type, size and count. getFileUrl resolves hosted, chunks: and legacy local: addresses and mirrors a fetched chunks: file into IndexedDB so each browser reads it once. firestore.rules gained a files match under users and under campaigns. Spark cannot bill: over quota it refuses. The 1 GiB store is the wall and the downscale is what keeps a table inside it.

q: Why was the profile empty on a page that mounts at load?
a: auth.init swapped getProfile for subscribeToProfile and stopped awaiting it, so isLoading went false before the first onSnapshot arrived. App.svelte renders the Router on !isLoading, so UserPage mounted with userProfile null and its onMount seeded displayName from nothing. Anything reactive still filled in later, which is why the email showed and the name did not. The subscription is now awaited for its first snapshot alongside getUserDetails before isLoading clears.

q: Where does the Replicate key live?
a: users/{uid}/data/details.replicate_api_key. The root users/{uid} document is readable by every signed in user (firestore.rules line 23, needed for party names and photos), so a secret on it was readable by anyone signed in. The data subtree is isOwner only. userService.putUserSecrets writes it, the userDetails store holds it, and ai.ts, chat.ts and Chat.svelte all read it from there. Never put it back on the profile document.

q: Why did uploads fail with Failed to process files?
a: public/pdf.worker.min.js was a July 2025 copy while pdfjs-dist is 6.3.289. pdf.js refuses a worker whose version does not match the API, so getDocument threw on every PDF. src/lib/sources.ts now resolves the worker from the installed package with import workerSrc from 'pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs?url', so it can never drift. The file in public/ is dead.

q: How are the menu and chat drawers opened?
a: From the Shell bar. MenuPanel and Chat each carried a position:absolute toggle at left:-50px / right:-50px, which the drawer aside clips with overflow:hidden, so neither drawer could be opened. Shell now holds menuOpen and chatOpen state, draws two Sigils in the bar, and sizes the grid columns from those. The --size-menu-curr and --size-chat-curr root variables are no longer written by anything.

q: What owns the page frame in dndcs?
a: src/components/ui/Shell.svelte. A 68px bar (crest or menu handle, back, title, nav snippet, profile chip, sign out, chat handle), optional menu and chat drawers driven by its own $state, a backdrop snippet layer, and a dnd-scroll content column held at narrow 860px, wide 1200px or full. Every authenticated page renders inside it. Page roots must never set their own 100vh or overflow-y: #app is absolute inset:0 overflow hidden, so a page that scrolls itself gets clipped.
